# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

@AGENTS.md

**Next.js 16.4 / React 19.3, plain CSS (no Tailwind).** Read the relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` before using framework APIs (e.g. `cookies()` is async). AGENTS.md is regenerated by `next dev`, so commit it rather than reverting it.

## Commands

```sh
npm run dev                 # dev server on :3000
npm run build               # production build
npm run lint                # eslint (flat config, eslint.config.mjs)
npx tsc --noEmit            # type check (not part of lint/build scripts)
npm run format              # prettier (120 columns); format:check verifies
npm test                    # node --test tests/*.test.mjs
node --test --test-name-pattern="single-day event" tests/reservation.test.mjs   # one test
```

Before calling work done, run all of these: lint, `tsc --noEmit`, `format:check`, tests, then build.

## Architecture

**Hotel marketing site plus a reservation-request system.** The app router lives in `src/app`. Public pages are `/`, `/rooms`, `/rooms/[slug]`, `/dining`, `/celebrations`, `/guest-information`, `/contact`, `/privacy` and `/book`. `/admin` is the staff dashboard (client-side), and `/login` is its login page. The `@/*` path alias maps to `src/*`.

**Reservations are requests, not bookings.** There is no payment, no live inventory and no automatic confirmation. Pending requests never block a room. Staff confirm everything manually. Keep UI copy and notification text in line with this: never promise availability or confirmation. Requests can cover 1–10 rooms and carry optional special requests (≤500 chars) and an optional offer code (checked against an active, in-date offer; stored in its own fields, shown on the offer card and pre-filled by its `/book?offer=…&code=…` link; codes are unique across offers and saved in capitals, a clash is a 409; requests saved before the code fields existed have it read out of their "Coupon CODE (Offer)" note). The hotel applies the offer when it confirms the rate. The amount shown is indicative and excludes taxes. Don't add payment/revenue UI.

**Rendering.** Public pages are server components. Pages that show stored content (`/`, `/rooms`, `/rooms/[slug]`, `/dining`, `/celebrations`) load it once on the server, pass it to components as props, and are statically generated with `revalidate = 300`. Admin writes call `revalidatePath("/", "layout")`, so changes appear on the next visit. Client components are only for real interactivity (header menu, `/book` form, gallery dialog, 3D tour, welcome gates, theme toggle, mobile reservation bar). The public site is English-only.

**Storage (`src/lib/db.ts`).** Two backends with identical behaviour, chosen by `DATABASE_URL`:

- Postgres (Neon). Required for Vercel production deploys: `next.config.ts` fails the build when `VERCEL_ENV=production` and `DATABASE_URL` is unset. Base tables come from `src/lib/db-schema.ts` (`initDB`, run via `/api/seed`, which needs admin auth plus `ALLOW_DATABASE_SEED=true`; it never seeds reviews). Newer columns/tables (`rooms_requested`, `special_requests`, `room_id`, `coupon_code`/`coupon_offer`, `notification_outbox` incl. `last_attempt_at`, `admin_state`, the room content columns) are added by additive DDL on first use; `/api/seed` also applies them up front via `prepareStorage()`.
- `data/db.json` (committed; content only, no guest data). Writes replace the file atomically; a corrupt file throws instead of being overwritten. On a read-only filesystem (e.g. Vercel without `DATABASE_URL`) reads fall back to built-in content and writes throw `StorageUnavailableError`, which routes turn into a 503.
- Enquiries, offers, banquet packages, dining options and reviews share one generic `collection()` implementation driven by a `CollectionDef` (field ↔ column map, encode/decode, sort order). To add a collection or field, extend its definition; both backends then store only declared fields. Bookings + outbox and rooms have their own code.
- Rooms are addressed by a stable `id` (Postgres: serial `idx`; JSON: derived from the name on first read). Never by list position or name. Each room record holds everything guests see: `slug` (its `/rooms/<slug>` address, unique, kept when the room is renamed; changing it stores the old one in `previousSlugs`, which the detail page 308-redirects), facts (`size`, `bed`, `occupancy`, `bathroom`, `location`, `view`; `""` = unapproved) and inclusions (`inRoom`, `services`). Staff edit all of it under Admin → Room Types; a slug clash is a 409. `image` is always the photo shown (no per-name overrides; `ILLUSTRATION_IMAGES` in `config.ts` controls the "Room illustration" label). Rooms stored before these fields existed are upgraded once (`prepareRooms()` / `normalizeRooms()`). Requests store `roomId` plus the name the guest saw; the calendar and analytics match by `roomId`, falling back to the name for older requests.

**Notification outbox.** `addBooking` writes the booking and an outbox row in the same step (a Postgres transaction, or one JSON write). `src/lib/notifications.ts` delivers pending events to `NOTIFICATION_WEBHOOK_URL`. It needs an HTTPS URL plus a secret of at least 32 characters. Each event carries an HMAC-SHA256 `X-Hotel-Signature` over `timestamp + '.' + body`, and delivery is at least once. When delivery isn't configured, events stay queued. `claimNotificationJobs()` picks due events (least-attempted first, then oldest) and stamps `lastAttemptAt` in the same step, so overlapping runs skip them; an event picked up in the last `NOTIFICATION_CLAIM_GUARD_MINUTES` (5) is never picked up again. After a failure an event waits `notificationRetryDelayMinutes()` (5 min doubling to 6 h); a staff retry from the dashboard (`/api/notifications`, `force: true`) skips that wait but not the guard. After `MAX_NOTIFICATION_ATTEMPTS` (8) failures an event becomes `failed` and admin can requeue it. Events whose request was deleted are discarded. Automatic retries run from Vercel Cron once a day (`vercel.json`) and every 10 minutes from `.github/workflows/scheduled-jobs.yml`. Both call `/api/cron/notifications`, which needs `CRON_SECRET` of at least 32 characters, refuses everything without it, and also runs the retention purge (`src/lib/retention.ts`; does nothing until `PRIVACY_INFORMATION.retentionMonths` is set).

**API routes (`src/app/api/*/route.ts`).**

- Admin collections (`rooms`, `offers`, `banquet`, `dining`, `reviews`) are one-liners over `adminCollectionRoute()` in `src/lib/admin-route.ts`: session check, validation against the schema in `src/lib/validation.ts` (unknown fields rejected), responses `{ item }` / `{ success }`, revalidation. A `ConflictError` from `db.ts` (room address or offer code already taken) becomes a 409 with its message. Only `rooms` and `banquet` have a public GET (filtered to visible/active, for the booking form).
- `bookings` and `enquiries` only allow status changes, except that staff can add a booking with `POST /api/bookings` (phone/desk bookings: same rules as `/api/book` via `contactError()`/`resolveStay()` in `src/lib/reservation.ts`, status `pending` or `confirmed`, an optional offer code under the same rule via `resolveCoupon()`, stored with `source: "staff"` and no notification-outbox row, so the guest gets no automatic message). There is no middleware/proxy: every admin handler checks the session itself (use the helpers in `admin-route.ts`).
- The only public write is `POST /api/book`, validated with `src/lib/reservation.ts` (Asia/Kolkata dates). A hidden `website` honeypot field gets a fake success and nothing is saved. The rate limiter (`src/lib/request-limit.ts`, per process) keys on the client address from the hosting proxy, never on form fields, and evicts instead of refusing when full. Logins count failures per address plus a higher per-account ceiling.
- Auth: `jose` HS256 JWT in the `admin_session` cookie; credentials from `ADMIN_EMAIL`/`ADMIN_PASSWORD`, compared in constant time; fails closed when `JWT_SECRET` is missing or shorter than 32 characters. Sessions last 8 h and carry a session version (`admin_state`, deliberately independent of the other tables so sign-in works before `/api/seed`); signing out bumps it, ending every session including copied tokens. If that fails, logout returns `revoked: false` and the dashboard warns.

**Admin dashboard.** Desktop-first. `src/app/admin/page.tsx` loads the data, owns request status changes/deletes and renders the shell; sections are addressed by the URL hash (`#requests`, `#requests/<id>`), so back/refresh keep the place. Pieces live in `src/components/admin/`: `Sidebar` (sections and badges), `Overview` (Today: reply queue oldest first, arrivals/departures), `RequestTable` (requests/enquiries: status chips, search, sort, detail panel with call/WhatsApp/email), `CalendarView` (month grid: stays as bars across their nights, laid out by `calendar-layout.ts`; clicking an empty future day opens `BookingForm`, a bar opens the request in a drawer), `BookingForm` (staff add-booking drawer), `CollectionEditor` (list + side drawer with grouped fields, configured per collection in `collections.tsx`), `Analytics` (no revenue), `SetupView` (notification outbox status + launch checklist), `ui.tsx` (toasts, confirm dialog, native `<dialog>` modal, `useNow`), `format.ts` (hotel-time dates, `fill`/`counted`), `status.tsx` (one tone per status meaning), `icons.tsx`. Styles are in `src/app/admin/admin.css` (tokens follow the site's light/dark theme; resets use `:where()` because the public `globals.css` styles bare `section`/`p`/headings, and avoid generic class names like `.bar` that globals already uses). `adminRequest()` throws on non-2xx, so the UI only changes after the server confirms. Every admin string is in `src/lib/i18n.ts` (en/hi, admin only).

**Content.**

- `src/lib/hotel-content.ts`: hotel policies, room-fact labels/`findRoom()`, and privacy-notice facts (`PRIVACY_INFORMATION`, rendered by `/privacy`). Unapproved facts stay `""`: guests never see them, and `missingLaunchDetails()` lists them in the admin launch checklist.
- `src/lib/config.ts`: site config, contact details and images. Representative images are flagged as samples.
- `src/lib/context.tsx`: the client `AppProvider` (theme, plus the admin's language).
- `src/lib/seo.ts`: Hotel JSON-LD built only from known facts.
- `public/images`: duplicates were removed; `src/lib/image-redirects.ts` redirects old filenames.

Theme is set through `data-theme` on `<html>`; an inline script in `layout.tsx` sets it before paint. Fonts come from `next/font` (`--font-display`, `--font-body`). Styles live in `globals.css` (ordered: tokens, base, components, sections, pages, motion, then one block per breakpoint 1100/900/600/360 (900 is split around the compact-height blocks), then reduced motion) and `hospitality.css`; `admin.css` is admin-only.

**Logging.** Server errors are logged as one JSON line (`src/lib/log.ts`; never guest details) and unhandled ones by `onRequestError` in `src/instrumentation.ts`.

**Security headers** (CSP, frame/sniff/referrer/permissions, HSTS) are set in `next.config.ts`. Scripts need `'unsafe-inline'` because pages are static; don't add third-party script or font origins without updating the CSP.

**SEO gating.** `robots`, `sitemap` and metadata stay non-indexable unless `SITE_READY_FOR_INDEXING=true`. `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` sets `metadataBase`. Contact details come from the `NEXT_PUBLIC_HOTEL_*` env vars (baked in at build time). Unset ones are hidden from guests, never shown as placeholder text, and appear in the admin launch checklist. Don't present sample reviews or photos as genuine: sample photos keep a short "representative photo" disclosure. Every page should set a `description`.

**Welcome gates.** `DoorIntro` plays once per browser session. The inline script in `layout.tsx` sets `<html data-welcome-seen>` before paint for returning visitors and same-site referrers, and CSS hides the gates, so they never flash. Any key, scroll or swipe skips them. If JavaScript never runs, a `<noscript>` style hides them, and a CSS-only failsafe animation hides them after 4s if hydration fails. See `.env.example` for all variables.

## Tests

`tests/reservation.test.mjs` doesn't use a framework or bundler. It transpiles TS source files with the `typescript` package and evaluates them with a stubbed `require`. Every import in the module under test must appear in the `mocks` map passed to `load()` (`@/lib/log` defaults to a silent logger). Otherwise the test throws `Unexpected dependency: <id>`. If you add an import to a route that has tests, update its mocks. Admin routes are loaded through the `adminRoute()` helper in the test file, which wires the real `validation` and `admin-route` modules to a fake db and session.
